author: blueiridium.
content: Hello I may have found a potential Gloas/ePBS spec bug if my testing and read of the situation are correct. EIP-7732 aims to protect an honest builder’s payload against proposer behavior. But in process_proposer_slashing (https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/master/specs/gloas/beacon-chain.md#modified-process_proposer_slashing ), the spec checks whether the proposer is still slashable before cancelling its builder payment. A proposer can sign conflicting blocks A and B, put its own attester slashing in canonical B, and cause the later A/B equivocation proof to be rejected. The builder’s payload was bound to A, yet B can remain EMPTY while its bid is paid. I reproduced this on a private five-node network: B and a 4.69 ETH test payment from builder escrow to a separate attacker account finalized. Public-network reliability and economics remain unmeasured. Thanks for taking a look.

author: potuz
content:
Hi, this is quite interesting and surely there can be edge cases with proposers slashing themselves. However I don't understand this one if the proposer slushes itself on say slot N, block A, and submits an equivocation: slot N block B. And suppose the slashing is included in B. The builder bid was included in A (I believe these are the parameters you considered).If the chain takes A as canonical then the proposer is not slashed in this chain, the payload in principle needs to be revealed, if builders don't then anyway any honest proposer that saw the slashing (the builder must have to not reveal so the builder broadcast the slashing) will include it and the builder will not pay. 

If otoh B becomes canonical then the builder doesn't even have a bid to pay.
